paper.title: Learning to Schedule Online Tasks with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online task scheduling with bandit feedback (reward-to-cost ratio maximization)
unmapped: Each pull yields both a stochastic reward and a stochastic positive cost; objective is the ratio of cumulative expected reward to cumulative expected cost
Task types (contexts) drawn i.i.d. from an unknown finite distribution over S types, each with its own finite decision set A(S_t)
Learner knows bounds r_max, c_min, theta_min, theta_max on mean rewards/costs
settings.definition_quote: We assume $S$ types of incoming tasks in the system ... every task is randomly drawn from a stationary probability distribution ... For the $t$th task, the controller observes its type $S_t \in \mathcal S$ and chooses a decision $a_t \in \mathcal A(S_t)$ ... the controller observes the feedback of reward $R_{S_t,a_t}$ and cost $C_{S_t,a_t}$ ... maximize the cumulative reward-to-cost ratio

conditions: Rewards sub-Gaussian with means in [r_min, r_max] (Assumption 1)
Costs positive sub-Gaussian with means in [c_min, c_max] (Assumption 2)
All (task type, decision) pairs explored once before decision making (footnote in proof)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assumption:reward} and~\ref{assumption:cost} hold, DOL-RM achieves the following regret: \mathcal{R}(T) = O(T^{\frac{3}{4}}).

results.notes: Regret defined as T * Gap(T), where Gap(T) = |theta* - sum E[R]/sum E[C]| is the gap between optimal and achieved reward-to-cost ratio; equivalently convergence gap O(T^{-1/4}). Not a standard regret, so quantity 'other'. Constants depend on r_max, c_min, theta range and sqrt(log T) (appendix C_2 contains sqrt(log T)), so the stated O hides a log factor.
